deep.reconstruction:
Context: a chapter on Fredholm theory (trace-class operators, here called 'applications de Fredholm', with norm ‖·‖₁) in Hilbert spaces, written around 1953. It feeds the analysis of the Fredholm coefficients α_n and of Weyl-type inequalities on the neighbouring pages. Grothendieck published this material in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 84, 1956).

Setting. Λⁿ E is the n-th exterior power of a Hilbert space E, with the Hilbert norm induced from E^{⊗n}. For operators u₁,…,u_n there is a mixed exterior product u₁∧…∧u_n: Λⁿ E → Λⁿ F. It is the symmetric multilinear polarization of u ↦ Λⁿ u, so that u∧…∧u = Λⁿ u.

Proposition 3. If each u_i is trace class from E to F, then u₁∧…∧u_n is trace class from ΛⁿE to ΛⁿF, and
  ‖u₁∧…∧u_n‖₁ ≤ (1/n!) ∏‖u_i‖₁.

Proof.
1. Trace-class operators form the projective tensor product Ē ⊗̂ F, whose unit ball is the closed convex hull of the rank-one tensors b̄⊗a with ‖a‖, ‖b‖ ≤ 1.
2. Hence it suffices to treat rank-one u_i = b̄_i⊗a_i. Then the multilinear map (u₁,…,u_n) ↦ u₁∧…∧u_n extends from (Ē⊗̂E)ⁿ to the trace class of ΛⁿE with norm ≤ 1/n!.
3. This extension agrees with the original map on decomposable tensors. Both maps are continuous into L(ΛⁿE), so they agree everywhere.
4. For rank-one factors, u₁∧…∧u_n = (1/n!)(b̄₁∧…∧b̄_n)⊗(a₁∧…∧a_n), citing formula (8) of N°1.
5. Hadamard's inequality ‖a₁∧…∧a_n‖ ≤ ∏‖a_i‖ (formula (5)) then gives the bound (13).

Corollary. For trace-class u on a Hilbert space E, Λⁿu is trace class and α_n(u) = Tr(Λⁿu) (formula (14)). Here α_n are the Fredholm coefficients of det(1+zu) = Σ α_n(u) zⁿ, defined in Chap. I. An earlier, struck-out version stated the multilinear form α_n(u₁,…,u_n) = Tr(u₁∧…∧u_n). The proof (checking on finite rank and extending by continuity) continues on the next page.

Next page. It derives:
- |α_n(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ (1/n!) ∏‖u_i‖₁;
- ‖Λⁿu‖₁ = α_n(|u|);
- ‖Λⁿu‖₂² = α_n(u*u).
All are standard Hilbert-space facts.
errors: No mathematical error. The 1/n! normalization is consistent. Taking u_i = rank-one projections onto orthonormal e_i, the coefficient of t₁…t_n in Λⁿ(Σ t_i p_i) is the projection onto e₁∧…∧e_n, so the mixed product is (1/n!)·P. Also, for a single u, ‖Λⁿu‖₁ = e_n(s_j(u)) ≤ (Σ s_j)ⁿ/n!.

The statement as transcribed says 'espaces de Banach', but the argument uses conjugate spaces b̄ and Hilbertian exterior powers. With the Hilbert reading the statement is correct; for genuine Banach spaces the clean 1/n! bound would fail (Grothendieck's Banach-space Fredholm theory carries extra factors like n^{n/2}).

ideas.what: Trace-norm estimate for mixed exterior products of trace-class operators, proved via the projective tensor product and Hadamard's inequality
ideas.modern_name: Bound ‖Λⁿu‖₁ ≤ ‖u‖₁ⁿ/n! (polarized form), e.g. Simon, Trace Ideals, Ch. 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Fredholm/Carleman estimates; Hilbert-space form in Grothendieck (1956), Simon (1977)
ideas.where_published: La théorie de Fredholm, Bull. SMF 84 (1956) 319–384 (and Produits tensoriels topologiques, 1955)

ideas.what: Fredholm coefficients as traces of exterior powers: α_n(u) = Tr Λⁿu, i.e. det(1+zu) = Σ zⁿ Tr Λⁿu
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Lidskii/Simon definition of the Fredholm determinant via exterior powers

ideas.what: Extension of multilinear identities from rank-one tensors to the whole projective tensor product by density and continuity
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the projective tensor product
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of standard material on Fredholm determinants via exterior powers in Hilbert space, which Grothendieck himself published in 1956 and which is now textbook (Simon). Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Soient E et F deux espaces de Banach' should very likely read 'deux espaces de Hilbert', given the conjugate b̄ and the Hilbertian Λⁿ.
Corollary: 'Soit E un espace de Banach' should likewise read 'Soit E un espace de Hilbert'.
'Mettre ici [?] les 2 et en Mason [?]' (red heading) is probably 'Mettre ici les … 2 et en …', an editorial note for rearranging the manuscript, not mathematics.
The domain in the proof should read (Ē⊗̂E)ⁿ → F̄⊗̂F with F = ΛⁿE, i.e. the trace class of ΛⁿE.
The final bound reads ≤ (1/n!) ∏‖a_i‖‖b_i‖, which is ≤ 1/n!.
